candidate.answerReason: The termwise sums form an arithmetic progression whose first and hundredth terms are both 100. Pairing its endpoints gives 50 pairs of sum 200, totaling 10,000.

methods.label: Pair terms of the combined progression
methods.explanation:
Adding corresponding terms preserves the constant-difference pattern. To see this, let \(c_k=a_k+b_k\), and let \(d_a,d_b\) be the common differences of the original progressions. Then
\[
c_{k+1}-c_k=d_a+d_b,
\]
which is constant. Thus \(c_1,c_2,\ldots\) is an arithmetic progression, with
\[
c_1=25+75=100,\qquad c_{100}=100.
\]
In an arithmetic progression, moving one step inward from the two ends increases one term by the common difference and decreases the other by the same amount. Consequently, each pair
\[
c_1+c_{100},\ c_2+c_{99},\ \ldots,\ c_{50}+c_{51}
\]
has sum \(200\). These 50 pairs include every one of the first 100 terms exactly once, so the required sum is
\[
50\cdot200=\boxed{10{,}000},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
